# Results — Study 863 (Treasury Noise Liquidity)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Hu, Pan &
Wang (2013), *"Noise as Information for Illiquidity"*: the cross-maturity **roughness** of the
Treasury yield curve is a market-wide illiquidity / funding-stress gauge (high noise = scarce
arbitrage capital), and high-noise regimes are said to **precede lower equity returns and wider
credit spreads**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped) — as-of 2026-06-30. Fingerprint `ecbb818e0905` (the four CMT yield columns).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **four CMT yield indices** `^IRX` (13w) / `^FVX` (5y) / `^TNX` (10y) / `^TYX` (30y) in %-points, plus `SPY` (equity, total-return), `HYG` (high-yield), `IEF` (7-10y Treasury hedge), `LQD`/`TLT` (reference), 2007-04-12 → 2026-06-30, **4,834** dated rows |
| Signal | daily **noise** = RMS deviation of the four yields from a **quadratic-in-maturity** fit (`y ≈ a + b·m + c·m²`); one constant residual-projection matrix `P⊥ = I − M(MᵀM)⁻¹Mᵀ`, so the whole series is a single matmul. Noise mean **0.094** %-pts (sd 0.063, max 0.394) |
| Targets | forward `h`-day cumulative log return of **SPY** and of **HYG − IEF** (daily high-yield-minus-Treasury credit-excess return); horizons `h ∈ {5, 21, 63}` trading days |
| Regression | OLS of the forward return on the **standardised** noise (`noise_z`, per-1σ slope) known at the close of day `t`, held `t → t+h`; **Newey-West (HAC)** slope *t* with lags = ⌈1.5·h⌉ |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: noise through close `t` → position held `t → t+h`. The regime timer charges one-way × NAV per switch (long-only; no borrow leg) |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) slope *t*; OLS *t*; a 3,000-draw block-rotation placebo (left-tail, the claim is a *negative* slope); a two-era cut (split 2016-01-01); a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The four CMT indices and the risk ETFs are
**continuously listed** (no delisting bias), and the noise measure is model-free (a fixed
quadratic fit) — so there is no cross-sectional survivorship inflation here. The one modelling
choice is the **risk-free leg proxied at 0** in the forward returns; a near-constant bill shifts
the regression *intercept*, not the *slope* that carries the *t*-stat.

## The headline — forward return regressed on noise (per 1σ)

Slope = forward return per 1σ of curve roughness; the claim (Hu-Pan-Wang) predicts a **negative**
slope for both targets.

**SPY (equity):**

| horizon | slope (%/1σ) | Newey-West *t* | OLS *t* | R² | hi−lo-noise third |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **5-day** | **−0.171** | **−2.20** | −4.75 | 0.47% | −0.29% |
| 21-day | −0.536 | −1.97 | −7.61 | 1.19% | −1.04% |
| 63-day | −0.755 | −1.03 | −6.52 | 0.88% | −1.62% |

**HYG − IEF (credit-excess):**

| horizon | slope (%/1σ) | Newey-West *t* | OLS *t* | R² | hi−lo-noise third |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day | −0.077 | −1.55 | −2.99 | 0.18% | −0.17% |
| 21-day | −0.206 | −1.29 | −3.94 | 0.32% | −0.51% |
| 63-day | +0.117 | +0.26 | +1.31 | 0.04% | −0.06% |

The sign is **exactly the claim's**: a rougher curve today precedes *lower* forward SPY and
(tighter → wider) *lower* HYG−IEF. The **SPY 5-day** leg clears the bar (NW *t* = −2.20); the
21-day is a near-miss (−1.97). The credit leg carries the right sign at short horizons but never
reaches significance under HAC errors (the daily overlap fattens the standard error).

## Robustness — two eras (split 2016-01-01)

| target / horizon | early slope (*t*) | late slope (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|
| SPY 5-day | −0.351 (**−2.42**, n=2,192) | −0.107 (−1.14, n=2,631) |
| SPY 21-day | −0.722 (−1.30) | −0.476 (−1.48) |
| HYG−IEF 5-day | −0.314 (**−2.54**) | +0.007 (+0.14) |
| HYG−IEF 21-day | (−1.86) | (+0.07) |

The entire edge lives in the **crisis-heavy 2007–2015 half** (GFC, Euro crisis, 2013 taper
tantrum, 2015 bund/China shocks). After 2016 the equity leg fades to insignificance and the
credit leg dies outright (a *flat* +0.14 / +0.07). **No sub-era clears |*t*| ≥ 2 at the monthly
horizon** — the hallmark of a stress-concentrated signal, not a durable premium.

## Placebo — is the (negative) slope a lucky alignment?

Circularly block-rotate the forward returns against the noise in 21-day blocks (preserves the
overlap autocorrelation), 3,000 draws; left-tail p (the claim is a *negative* slope):

| target / horizon | position of observed | left-tail p |
|---|--:|--:|
| SPY 5-day | **−2.39σ** into the left tail | **0.0083** |
| SPY 21-day | −1.88σ | 0.0303 |
| HYG−IEF 5-day | −1.46σ | 0.0393 |
| HYG−IEF 21-day | −0.96σ | 0.1603 |

The SPY 5-day slope is a genuine left-tail event (p ≈ 0.008), not a rotation artefact; the credit
21-day sits inside the null cloud. Consistent with the era cut: real, but shallow.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Own SPY over `t → t+1` when the noise known at `t−1` is **below** its expanding median (calm curve
⇒ own the market), else cash; one-way cost per switch, no borrow leg.

| one-way cost | timer Sharpe | buy-and-hold Sharpe | timer − B&H | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | 0.311 | 0.528 | **−2.53 bps/day** | −2.14 |
| 3 bps | 0.292 | 0.528 | −2.63 bps/day | −2.23 |

The timer **significantly underperforms buy-and-hold** (Sharpe 0.31 vs 0.53; −2.5 bps/day, NW
*t* = −2.1), churning 12.7×/yr and invested only 43% of the time. The reason is mechanical: noise
spikes **coincide** with the drawdown rather than leading it by enough, so stepping out on rough
days mostly forfeits the rebound. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded tape: a persistent AR(1) noise level scales per-maturity curve deviations
(so roughness recovers it) and — with `edge>0` — drags the *next* day's SPY / HYG−IEF mean return
down. No network.

| world | SPY 21-day slope NW *t* | fires (\|*t*\|≥2) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.17** | **0/20** |
| planted (`edge = 0.03`, SPY) | **−7.33** (slope −1.77%/1σ, R² 10.2%) | 20/20 |
| planted (`edge = 0.05`, credit) | **−10.41** | 20/20 |

The detector recovers a planted noise→return relation cleanly for both targets and **never fires
on the null** — so the real-tape decay is a genuine feature of the tape, not a biased estimator.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The Hu-Pan-Wang Treasury-noise measure has the **right sign** (a rough curve
  precedes weaker equity and wider credit) and is **full-tape significant and placebo-real at the
  short horizon** (SPY 5-day NW *t* = **−2.20**, −2.39σ in a 3,000-draw placebo), with a 21-day
  near-miss (−1.97). But the edge is **concentrated in the crisis-heavy 2007–2015 era** (SPY 5d
  *t* = −2.42) and **decays to insignificance after 2016** (*t* = −1.14); no sub-era clears
  |*t*| ≥ 2 at the monthly horizon, and the credit leg fires **only in the GFC** (−2.54 → +0.14).
  A right-signed, genuinely stress-informative gauge that is **not certifiable out of sample.**
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A noise-conditioned long/flat SPY timer **loses to buy-and-hold**
  (Sharpe 0.31 vs 0.53; −2.53 bps/day, NW *t* = −2.14) — the noise coincides with the crash rather
  than leading it, so there is no paycheck in stepping aside.
- **In-sample vs out-of-sample — DECAYED.** A ~2.4-*t* crisis-era edge collapses to an
  insignificant −1.1 after 2016 — a post-publication / post-QE fade.
